 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani
 Order

By way of the present petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India and read with section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1973, the petitioner seeks quashing of case FIR No. 61/2014 dated 22.01.2014 registered under section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ('IPC') at P.S.: Kanjhawala, in which chargesheet has been filed adding sections 467/468/471 IPC.
2.

The quashing is based on settlement terms stated to have been agreed to between the petitioner and respondent No.2 on 23.08.2019, towards which settlement the sum of Rs.4.5 lacs stands paid by the petitioner to respondent No. 2.
3.
In addition to the affidavit of the petitioner, the petition is also supported by an affidavit of respondent No.2.

The petitioner and respondent No.2 are present in court; and on being queried,
they unequivocally support the settlement.

4. The essence of the allegation in the FIR, and subsequently in the chargesheet, is that the petitioner entered into a transaction to sell a property owned by his mother to respondent No.2;
whereas the mother had sold that property to a third party.
5. It is not immediately clear if, in the process, the petitioner forged or tampered with any public record or any stamp paper.

sentences.text: In view of the above, before proceeding further with the matter, in order to obtain clarity on the aforesaid aspect and to assess if there are any wider public law implications in the case, issue notice.
7. Mr. Yasir Rauf Ansari, learned ASC appears for the State on advance copy; accepts notice; and seeks time to file status report.

8. Let status report be filed within 06 weeks; response thereto, if any, be filed within 04 weeks thereafter; with copies to the opposing counsel.
9. Re-notify on 20th September 2023.
